critical_policy_flags: SNAP ABAWD work requirements active statewide
Ohio minimum wage $10.45/hr — far below living wage
Ohio Works First 36-month lifetime limit (shorter than federal 60)
Ohio eviction timeline 3-day notice + 10-14 day total
Ohio UI appeal deadline 21 days (shorter than IL/NY 30 days)
OCRC 2-year civil rights SOL (broader than federal 300 days)

programs.eligibility: Income < 130% FPL statewide. Ohio SNAP administered through 88 county JFS offices. ABAWD work requirement active — 80 hrs/month ages 18-54.
programs.apply_notes: Apply at benefits.ohio.gov (online) or local county JFS office. Expedited service within 7 days if income < $150/mo or housing costs exceed income. Summer EBT (SUN Bucks) available for school-aged children.

programs.eligibility: Franklin County and surrounding counties — 500+ partner agencies.
programs.apply_notes: midohiofoodbank.org — largest food bank in Ohio, serves 20-county area around Columbus. SNAP enrollment assistance also available.

programs.eligibility: Cuyahoga, Ashtabula, Geauga, Lake, and Ashland counties.
programs.apply_notes: greaterclevelandfoodbank.org — largest food bank in Northeast Ohio.

programs.eligibility: Hamilton, Butler, Clermont, Warren, and Boone counties (including KY border counties).
programs.apply_notes: freestorefoodbank.org — serves tri-state area (OH/KY/IN). Cincinnati area addresses cross-state resource complexity.

programs.eligibility: Pregnant, postpartum women, infants, children under 5 — income < 185% FPL.
programs.apply_notes: odh.ohio.gov/wic — find local WIC clinic by county. Federal program, same eligibility nationwide.

programs.program_name: Ohio Medicaid / Healthy Start / Healthy Families (ODM)
programs.eligibility: Adults 19-64 to 138% FPL (expanded). Families, children (Healthy Start), pregnant women, seniors, disability. NO coverage gap.
programs.apply_notes: Apply at benefits.ohio.gov — one application for SNAP, Medicaid, and cash. Managed care plans: CareSource, Molina, Buckeye Health Plan, Anthem, UnitedHealthcare Community Plan.

programs.eligibility: Cuyahoga County residents — comprehensive public hospital and clinic system, charity care, sliding scale.
programs.apply_notes: metrohealth.org — Level 1 trauma center + 20+ community health centers in Cuyahoga County. No one turned away.

programs.eligibility: Columbus residents — sliding scale primary care, STI, maternal health, immunizations.
programs.apply_notes: columbus.gov/publichealth — locate nearest Columbus Public Health clinic. Also HealthPath (614-443-8500) and Equitas Health (614-294-5531) for LGBTQ+ affirming care.

programs.eligibility: Anyone regardless of insurance — sliding scale primary, dental, behavioral health.
programs.apply_notes: findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov — 60+ FQHCs statewide. Key: OhioHealth FQHCs Columbus, Neighborhood Health Plan Mahoning Valley (Youngstown 330-746-3231), Cincinnati Health Dept FQHCs (513-357-7310).

programs.eligibility: Ohioans unable to afford prescriptions — medication assistance program navigator.
programs.apply_notes: needymeds.org — free national resource for pharmaceutical assistance programs. Ohio also has bulk discount programs through managed care plans.

programs.program_name: Ohio Housing Finance Agency (OHFA) — Emergency Rental Assistance
programs.eligibility: Low-income Ohio renters facing eviction — income < 80% AMI. Program availability varies by county and funding cycle.
programs.apply_notes: ohiohome.org — OHFA coordinates state-level rental assistance and Section 8/HCV waiting lists. Local administering agencies handle direct applications.

programs.eligibility: Franklin County — Section 8 Housing Choice Vouchers, public housing.
programs.apply_notes: cmhanet.com — HCV waiting list opens periodically. Also Cuyahoga MHA (216-348-5000), Cincinnati MHA (513-721-4580).

programs.eligibility: Franklin and surrounding counties — housing, family, benefits, DV, consumer, immigration.
programs.apply_notes: columbuslegalaid.org — same-day triage for eviction cases given Ohio's fast eviction timeline. Call immediately upon receipt of any notice.

programs.eligibility: Cuyahoga, Lake, Geauga, Ashtabula counties — housing, family, benefits, DV, consumer, elder.
programs.apply_notes: lasclev.org — largest legal aid in Northeast Ohio.

programs.eligibility: Hamilton, Clermont, Warren, Butler counties and NKY border counties — housing, family, benefits.
programs.apply_notes: lascinti.org — tri-state area; also handles Kentucky border county referrals.

programs.eligibility: Summit, Stark, Portage, Tuscarawas, and Mahoning counties — housing, family, benefits.
programs.apply_notes: communitylegalaid.org — intake covers Northeast Ohio outside Cuyahoga. Key for Akron, Canton, Youngstown corridor.

programs.program_name: Ohio State Legal Services Association / Ohio Legal Help
programs.eligibility: Statewide — free civil legal information, triage, referral to local legal aid offices.
programs.apply_notes: ohiolegalhelp.org — Ohio's central legal aid intake and self-help portal. Equivalent of illinoislegalaid.org.

programs.program_name: Advocates for Basic Legal Equality (ABLE) — NW Ohio
programs.eligibility: Lucas, Wood, Fulton, Henry, Ottawa, Sandusky, Erie, Defiance, Williams, Paulding, Van Wert counties — Toledo area.
programs.apply_notes: ablelaw.org — primary legal aid for Northwest Ohio including Toledo corridor. Also Farmworker Legal Services: migrant/seasonal farmworker cases throughout OH.

programs.eligibility: Athens, Gallia, Hocking, Jackson, Lawrence, Meigs, Morgan, Monroe, Noble, Perry, Vinton, Washington counties — Appalachian Ohio.
programs.apply_notes: seols.net — covers rural Appalachian Ohio southeast of Columbus. Critical region for poverty, opioid crisis intersection, and rural housing.

programs.eligibility: 24/7 statewide — crisis support, shelter referral, safety planning.
programs.apply_notes: odvn.org — Ohio DV coalition coordinates 75+ local DV programs. Also Ohio Sexual Violence Hotline (877-644-6435). Text START to 88788.

programs.eligibility: Families with children, income < 50% FPL — up to $536/month family of 3. 36-month Ohio lifetime limit (shorter than federal 60).
programs.apply_notes: Apply at benefits.ohio.gov or county JFS. Verify remaining months for any prior Ohio TANF recipient — 36-month clock is FATAL. Work requirement 30 hrs/week. Never standalone — pair with SNAP, Medicaid, CCAP, HEAP.

programs.agency: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services
programs.eligibility: Workers who lost job through no fault — up to $660/week, 26 weeks (may be fewer based on base period wages).
programs.apply_notes: unemployment.ohio.gov — file online. 21-day appeal deadline from mailing date — FATAL and shorter than neighboring states. Contact legal aid within 10 days of any denial.

programs.eligibility: Income < 175% FPL — heating, cooling (Summer Crisis Program), crisis shutoff prevention, weatherization (HWAP).
programs.apply_notes: energyhelp.ohio.gov — apply through local Community Action Agency. Opens November 1 for heating season. Summer Crisis Program: July 1-August 31. Crisis component year-round for imminent shutoffs. Find local CAA: communityactionohio.org.
